subject: literature
passage: For as long as Zara could remember, her grandfather had kept a typewriter repair shop on a side street in ______ a narrow room lined with shelves of spare keys, ribbons, and rollers. Few customers came anymore, but every machine that did arrive left the shop with its letters striking the page as evenly as the day it was made.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A narrow room lined with shelves of spare keys, ribbons, and rollers" is not a sentence; it is a phrase that renames the shop. Such a phrase is attached to the end of a sentence with a comma.
explanation.A: Correct. The comma attaches the phrase that renames the shop to the end of the sentence.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "A narrow room lined with shelves of spare keys, ribbons, and rollers" has no verb and can't stand as a sentence on its own; this creates a fragment.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on each side; the describing phrase is not a clause.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the describing phrase runs into "Rawalpindi" with nothing to connect it to the shop.
